title: observability: automate prometheus/grafana + logs for private installs
author: Priya Patel
release_notes: Add automated observability bootstrap for Private installs: Helm charts for Prometheus/Grafana, Terraform module wiring, Filebeat/Fluentd defaults, and bundled dashboards/alerts. Backwards compatible by default; opt-in via installer flag.
description:
Motivation:
Enable a one-click (opt-in) observability bootstrap for Private installs (VPC/on-prem) to reduce manual setup time and support consistent defaults across customers. This PR wires Helm charts, a Terraform module, installer flags, and example manifests for Prometheus, Grafana, and log shipping (Filebeat/Fluentd).

What this changes:
- Adds a new Helm chart (helm/redwood-observability) that installs Prometheus Operator CRDs, Prometheus instances, Grafana with preloaded dashboards, and a lightweight Filebeat daemonset for log shipping. Values default to disabled; installer flips the flag when requested.
- Terraform module (terraform/modules/observability) exposes inputs for storageClass, retention, external Grafana credentials, and network policies for VPC peering. The module is wired into the installer templates to create required PVCs and IAM roles where applicable.
- Installer changes: new --enable-observability flag, observability-defaults.yaml, and an upgrade script (installer/upgrade/observability-migrate.sh) to backfill configs into existing clusters during upgrades.
- Bundled dashboards and alerts: dashboards/redwood-overview.json and alerts/redwood-slo-alerts.yaml created from our internal SLOs.
- Docs: docs/private/observability-setup.md with step-by-step and troubleshooting.

Commits (high-level):
- c1a9f4b: scaffold helm chart and basic templates
- d34b2a1: add Grafana provisioning + dashboards
- f7e1240: Filebeat daemonset + log parsing pipelines
- a0b9c6e: Terraform module and variables
- b3c8d99: installer flag + defaults + example manifest
- e5d7a20: upgrade script + migration path + docs

Files changed (high level):
- Helm chart and templates for Prometheus/Grafana/log shipping
- Terraform observability module + references in installer pipeline
- Installer flags, defaults, upgrade script, and example manifests
- Dashboards and alert rules exported from Grafana team
- Docs and quickstart for private observability

Testing and validation:
- Local k3s smoke tests: installed observability chart with default values, verified Prometheus scrape targets and Grafana dashboards load (tested on k3s v1.28).
- E2E on a staging VPC: deployed with terraform module, validated PVC creation, network policies, and Filebeat → ELK pipeline ingestion.
- CI: helm lint, terraform validate, bash unit tests for installer flag parsing. All checks passed on the final run.
- Load test: Prometheus instance configured with 1-week retention handled 600k samples/hour in staging; Grafana UI responsive under typical load.

Backward compatibility and rollout:
- Observability is opt-in by default (disabled). Customers upgrading will not get observability enabled unless they set --enable-observability or the new field in installer config.
- The upgrade script will detect prior incomplete installs and migrate user-provided values to the new charts without data loss.

Security considerations:
- Grafana is deployed behind the customer ingress; default admin password is randomized and stored in a Kubernetes secret. Documentation includes recommended KMS/HSM integration for secrets.
- Network policies restrict scraping to the Prometheus service account and cluster-internal CIDRs. Terraform module documents required IAM roles for cloud environments.

Review notes / open questions:
- We default to Filebeat for log shipping; some customers prefer Fluentd. The chart includes a toggle; we opted for Filebeat as the default for resource efficiency, but we can add a Fluentd subchart if adoption requires it.
- Long-retention customers should offload to remote_write targets; we added terraform variables to configure remote_write endpoints.

Review conversation (summary):
- Liam O'Connor: "Nice end-to-end. Two asks: (1) add an e2e test that validates alerts firing for SLO breach; (2) make Grafana provisioning secrets compatible with our vault-migrator."
- Priya Patel (author): "Added an e2e alert smoke test and integrated vault-migrator secret path. See commits f7e1240 -> e5d7a20 for changes."
- Sofia Martinez: "Please double-check network policy for multi-az clusters; I'm seeing a potential pod->pod block in our staging run."
- Priya Patel: "Adjusted policies to allow kube-system DNS and cross-az node CIDRs; validated in staging."
- Ethan Zhou: "CI lint failure initially on helm templates; fixed by templating storageClass and making pvc optional when using remote write."
- Reviewer approvals: Liam (approved), Sofia (approved after re-run), Ethan (approved).

CI status and checks:
- GitHub Actions: helm-lint (pass), terraform-validate (pass), installer-unit (pass), e2e-staging (pass, reran once), security-scan (pass).

Migration & rollback plan:
- Migration: installer/upgrade/observability-migrate.sh will detect old configs and apply migrations. Customers running older installers will be prompted during upgrade to opt-in to observability migration with a dry-run output.
- Rollback: charts include reversible changes; disabling observability will scale down components and preserve PVCs. For critical failures, operator can set helm --wait false and helm uninstall --keep-history to rollback. Documented in docs/private/observability-setup.md.

Conclusion:
This PR adds a fully-tested, opt-in observability automation path for Private installs, reducing manual setup for customers while keeping defaults conservative. Asking for squash merge once CI completes (all green).
notes: This PR was part of the ENG-4821 observability automation epic and coordinated with the Grafana team for dashboard exports. No breaking changes to existing installs unless customer enables the feature.
changelog_entry: Added opt-in observability bootstrap for Private installs (Prometheus/Grafana/Filebeat) with Terraform module, Helm chart, dashboards, alerts, and installer integration.
approximate_impact: Improves first-time setup time for observability from multiple hours of manual config to a single opt-in step; reduces ops runbook complexity for Private customers.
